newsitem.title: UK: Extradited British army deserter jailed for bomb.
newsitem.headline: Extradited British army deserter jailed for bomb.

text.p: A British army deserter extradited from the United States to face trial for an IRA bombing more than 22 years ago was jailed for 14 years on Thursday.
Lawyers said Peter McMullen, 49, could be freed soon, however, because of the time he spent in jail while in the U.S. before his extradition and while in pre-trial detention in Britain.
McMullen, a former cook with the Parachute Regiment who joined the guerrilla Irish Republican Army, had pleaded guilty to the bombings.

He admitted planting four bombs in the English headquarters of another regiment which had many soldiers serving in Northern Ireland at the time. Three of the bombs went off, injuring a woman. About 100 soldiers escaped injury in the blast.
McMullen had fought extradition from the United States since 1978. He finally gave up his fight in March and flew back from New York escorted by British police.

Under normal rules McMullen would have served nine years and eight months of his 14-year sentence. The judge allowed to be set against that nine years and three months in custody in the U.S. and the time spent in custody in Britain since his return.
"This was a bad case," Judge Arthur Myerson of York Crown Court told McMullen. "It was carefully planned by you and it was daringly executed."

But Myerson noted that McMullen, now said to be under an IRA death sentence for refusing to carry out a later robbery and kidnapping, had since publicly renounced the guerrilla group and all violence.
